title: Singapore Holds Monetary Policy as Economy Expands 5.4% on AI
source_used: Bloomberg (opening paragraphs, paywalled) and AsiaOne's full report of the MAS statement and GDP figures
key_facts: The Monetary Authority of Singapore kept the slope, width and centre of its policy band unchanged on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026, its first pause after tightening in April and July (Bloomberg).
Bloomberg: the central bank expects both the global energy crunch and the AI boom to ease up in 2027.
Ten analysts polled by Reuters had all expected a tightening (AsiaOne).
Singapore's GDP grew 5.4% in Q3 2026 from a year earlier, slower than 6.2% in Q2; quarter on quarter, 1.1% against 1.5% (AsiaOne).
MAS expects steady expansion before AI-related activity eases in the second half of 2027.
Core inflation rose to 2.1% in July and August; MAS forecasts core inflation of 1.5% to 2% for 2026 and 1.5% to 2.5% for 2027.
MAS said 'the risks to inflation remain tilted to the upside'.
quote_evidence: Singapore's central bank unexpectedly left monetary policy unchanged as it expects both the global energy crunch and the artificial-intelligence boom to ease up in 2027.
Ten analysts polled earlier by Reuters had all expected a tightening.
The central bank said Singapore's economy is expected to continue expanding steadily before the pace of AI-related activity eases in the second half of 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: Singapore's central bank sees AI-driven growth easing in 2027 and paused its tightening.
notes: Bloomberg prefetch holds only the first two paragraphs (paywall); the statement details and GDP figures were read in AsiaOne's full report. 'Unexpectedly' is Bloomberg's word and is supported by the Reuters poll AsiaOne cites.
